title_en: Character Riddles (17/20): A Hand Above the Eyes
note_en: 看 is normally kàn, "to look," but when it means "to watch over" it's read kān, in the first tone, as in 看守 "to guard," 看护 "to nurse," and 看家 "to mind the house." The text also shows how 看 combines into everyday words whose meaning drifts away from "looking": 看法 "opinion," 好看 "good-looking," 看重 "to value highly."
